'''''Cruelty Squad''''' is a 2021 [[Tactical shooter|tactical]] [[first-person shooter]] developed and published by Finnish<ref>{{cite web |url=https://twitter.com/CSoftproducts |title=Consumer Softproducts Oy (@CSoftproducts) |website=Twitter |type=Twitter profile with a location specified |language=en |access-date=2022-08-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709190704/https://twitter.com/CSoftproducts |archive-date=2021-07-09 |url-status=live |quote=Helsinki, Finland.}}</ref> [[Indie game|indie]] studio Consumer Softproducts, managed by artist Ville Kallio. In the game, the player takes on the role of a [[Human enhancement|biologically-augmented]] [[assassin]] employed by the titular [[wetwork]] [[security company]], tasked with performing [[black operations]] for its host conglomerate.<ref name="PCGamer rev">{{Cite magazine |last=Davenport |first=James |date=2021-07-02 |title=Cruelty Squad review |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/cruelty-squad-review/ |url-status=live |department=Review |magazine=PC Gamer |language=en |publisher=Future plc |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210705181125/https://www.pcgamer.com/cruelty-squad-review/ |archive-date=2021-07-05 |access-date=2022-08-04}}</ref> The game is notable for its [[Surrealism|surreal]], "sensorally aggressive"<ref name="RPS" /> aesthetic.

''Cruelty Squad'' is described by the developer as "an immersive power fantasy simulator with tactical stealth elements",<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Bruce-Jones |first=Henry |date=2021-03-03 |title=Ville Kallio finds the violence in corporate infrastructure in Cruelty Squad |url=https://www.factmag.com/2021/03/03/ville-kallio-cruelty-squad/ |url-status=live |magazine=Fact Magazine |language=en |publisher=The Vinyl Factory |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415014525/https://www.factmag.com/2021/03/03/ville-kallio-cruelty-squad/ |archive-date=2021-04-15 |access-date=2022-08-04}}</ref> and has been compared to games such as ''[[Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six (video game)|Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six]]'', ''[[Deus Ex (video game)|Deus Ex]]'', and ''[[Hitman: Codename 47]]''.<ref name="PCGamer rev" /><ref name="RPS" /><ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Marshall |first=Cass |date=2021-07-27 |title=Cruelty Squad is both brilliant and hard to love |url=https://www.polygon.com/reviews/22596014/cruelty-squad-immersive-sim-review-missions-combat-aesthetics |access-date=2023-05-20 |website=Polygon |language=en-US}}</ref> The game's themes have been described as [[anti-capitalist]], [[anti-corporate]], and a [[satire]] on the [[gig economy]].<ref name="PCGamer rev" /><ref name="Bloody" /><ref name="NME" />

The game was released in [[early access]] on Steam on 4 January 2021, and was fully released on Steam on 15 June 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cruelty Squad on Steam |url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1388770/Cruelty_Squad/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210418172808/https://store.steampowered.com/app/1388770/Cruelty_Squad/ |archive-date=2021-04-18 |access-date=2022-08-04 |website=Steam |language=en |type=Steam store page |quote=Release Date: 15 Jun, 2021 / Early Access Release Date: 4 Jan, 2021.}}</ref> Reviews were largely positive, with many reviewers appreciating the game's unique presentation, design, and combination of different mechanics and themes.

== Gameplay ==
The player chooses their weaponry and equipment before starting each of the 19 missions present in the game, and then must traverse open, [[Sandbox game|sandbox-style]] levels to locate and neutralize targets.<ref name="PCGamer">{{Cite magazine |last=Davenport |first=James |date=2021-01-11 |title=Cruelty Squad is a depressing Rainbow Six fever dream |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/cruelty-squad-is-a-depressing-rainbow-six-fever-dream/ |url-status=live |magazine=[[PC Gamer]] |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309221456/https://www.pcgamer.com/cruelty-squad-is-a-depressing-rainbow-six-fever-dream/ |archive-date=2021-03-09 |access-date=2021-03-31}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{cite news |last=Reuben |first=Nic |date=2021-07-01 |title=Cruelty Squad review: this game is too cool for me, probably |language=en |work=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]] |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/cruelty-squad-review |access-date=2021-07-06}}</ref> Health lost during combat can be regained by using certain equipment, consuming cooked giblets, or even eating corpses should the player die enough times on a level ("Power In Misery", the easiest [[difficulty level]]). While there is no penalty for killing civilians during a mission, silent and non-lethal solutions are also possible outside of the necessary killing of targets.<ref name="Bloody">{{Cite web |last=Andrew King |date=2021-02-16 |title='Cruelty Squad' is the Shooter '90s Parents Were Worried About |url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/video-games/3652204/cruelty-squad-shooter-90s-parents-worried/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610130033/https://bloody-disgusting.com/video-games/3652204/cruelty-squad-shooter-90s-parents-worried/ |archive-date=2022-06-10 |access-date=2021-03-31 |website=Bloody Disgusting! |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Cruelty Squad: Skurriler Taktik-Shooter verlässt den Early Access|url=https://www.4players.de/4players.php/spielinfonews/PC-CDROM/42669/2198792/Cruelty_Squad-Skurriler_Taktik-Shooter_verlaesst_den_Early_Access.html|access-date=2021-06-18|website=4Players|date=17 June 2021 |language=de|archive-date=2022-06-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610130040/https://www.4players.de/4players.php/spielinfonews/PC-CDROM/42669/2198792/Cruelty_Squad-Skurriler_Taktik-Shooter_verlaesst_den_Early_Access.html|url-status=live}}</ref> During missions, the player can harvest organs from corpses as well as go fishing, then they can trade those organs and fish on a dynamic [[stock market]] for money, or explore Cruelty Squad's headquarters.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Alex |date=2021-07-06 |title=Cruelty Squad Is The Video Game Equivalent Of A Contact High |url=https://www.kotaku.com.au/2021/07/cruelty-squad-steam-acid-trip-deus-ex/ |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610130034/https://www.kotaku.com.au/2021/07/cruelty-squad-steam-acid-trip-deus-ex/ |archive-date=2022-06-10 |access-date=2021-07-06 |website=[[Kotaku Australia]] |language=en-AU}}</ref>

== Plot ==
''Cruelty Squad'' is set in a dystopian [[corporatocracy]] where corporations possess overwhelming influence over police and government affairs. Technological advances allow people to be resurrected after death, rendering much of humanity immortal and cheapening the perceived value of life. Indiscriminate killings are commonplace, and armed security is a fixture of virtually every populated area. Human and animal organs are sold on the stock market, and invasive biological implants and augmented organs are used by security forces and assassins to aid in combat. Corporate [[contract killings]] are handled in part by Cruelty Squad, a wetwork security company working under the umbrella of a large [[conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]].

After being discharged from the "[[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission|SEC]] Death Unit", the [[player character]] -whom sports bright, neon colored atire, as well as matching colored [[norwood scale|receding hair]]- receives a phone call from his [[Agent handler|handler]], who offers him employment within Cruelty Squad. He is tasked to kill a number of people who have drawn the ire of conglomerate "higher-ups"; these include anti-corporate politicians, cultists, rogue police officers, delinquent employees, and rival CEOs. Eventually, the handler attempts to put a hit out on the player in their apartment, forcing the player to escape other assassins and police officers, however the handler apologizes and claims it was a mistake. Later in the game, the player and his handler begin to turn on the higher-ups, not due to any real anti-corporate beliefs, but simply for the [[Black comedy|potential humor]] of the situation.

The game features multiple endings depending on the player's discoveries. By activating the "Hope Eradicated" difficulty mode hidden within the Cruelty Squad headquarters, a sealed door opens, leading the protagonist to face a boss resembling themselves. Defeating this entity triggers the first ending.
Alternatively, completing a series of secret levels concealed within paintings unlocks the final level, "Trauma Loop". Here, an entity known as the Limit Chancellor strips the protagonist of their weapons and augmentations. Successfully navigating this level without equipment leads to the game's final ending.

== Development ==
''Cruelty Squad'' was produced within the [[Godot (game engine)|Godot game engine]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Klepek |first1=Patrick |title=Good Luck Finding a Stranger, More Interesting Game in 2021 Than 'Cruelty Squad' |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/good-luck-finding-a-stranger-more-interesting-game-in-2021-than-cruelty-squad/ |website=Vice.com |date=September 7, 2021 |access-date=18 September 2023}}</ref> It was released on Steam on 15 June 2021.

Prior to the development of ''Cruelty Squad'', lead developer and artist Ville Kallio created and exhibited multiple artistic works consisting of comics and [[video art]], as well as installations and standalone artworks for galleries. Notable museums he has exhibited include the Futura in [[Prague]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-06-03 |title=Ville Kallio and Bora Akinciturk at Futura |url=https://artviewer.org/ville-kallio-and-bora-akinciturk-at-futura/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610130034/https://artviewer.org/ville-kallio-and-bora-akinciturk-at-futura/ |archive-date=2022-06-10 |access-date=2022-05-13 |website=ArtViewer.org}}</ref> and the SIC Gallery in [[Helsinki, Finland]].<ref name="ofluxo">{{Cite web |date=13 February 2020 |title=Venmo Combat Ville Kallio At SIC Gallery, Helsinki, Finland |url=https://www.ofluxo.net/venmo-combat-ville-kallio-at-sic-gallery-helsinki/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210908040658/https://www.ofluxo.net/venmo-combat-ville-kallio-at-sic-gallery-helsinki/ |archive-date=2021-09-08 |access-date=2022-05-13 |website=fluxo}}</ref> Many of these previous artworks contain allusions to video games, as well as many ideas that would later become parts of ''Cruelty Squad''. Kallio has said that his gallery work "never really felt like more than just a weird hobby" and that it was like "a black hole with no future", stating that going into game development felt sensible since his previous work had been heavily inspired by video games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Good |first=Christopher |date=2021-08-19 |title=ARTIST OF THE WEEK Ville Kallio |url=https://lvl3official.com/ville-kallio/ |access-date=2022-05-13 |website=LVL3Official |archive-date=2021-08-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210823184305/https://lvl3official.com/ville-kallio/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Other than gallery pieces, Kallio has produced many video projects before the release of ''Cruelty Squad'', such as "Adversalife"<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VUc0HYtGoFE "Adversalife"] YouTube</ref> and "Venmo Combat"<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pwd9smKsEns "Venmo Combat"] YouTube</ref> which was also a component of a multimedia art exhibition hosted at the SIC Gallery in Helsinki, Finland.<ref name="ofluxo" /> Additionally, he worked on comics such as ''Hyper Prison-Industrial'',<ref>[https://zco.mx/VilleKallio/HYPERPRISONINDUSTRIAL ''Hyper Prison-Industrial''] zco.mx</ref> ''Bio-whale,''<ref>[https://www.peow.studio/shop/bio-whale ''Bio-whale'']</ref> ''Corridorspace,''<ref>[https://zco.mx/VilleKallio/CORRIDORSPACE ''Corridorspace''] zco.mx</ref> and developed a second game titled ''[[Psycho Patrol R]]'' in 2025 through [[early access]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Egan |first=Toussaint |date=2025-04-01 |title=Cruelty Squad creator's latest is a nightmare cop sim where social media is a drug and you pilot a mech with chicken legs |url=https://www.polygon.com/impressions/549723/psycho-patrol-r-cyberpunk-immersive-sim-mech-shooter |access-date=2025-04-25 |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]}}</ref>

== Reception ==
{{Video game reviews
| PCGUS = 93/100<ref>{{cite web |last1=Davenport |first1=James |title=Cruelty Squad review |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/cruelty-squad-review/ |website=[[PC Gamer]] |date=2 July 2021 |access-date=25 November 2021 |archive-date=10 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610130035/https://www.pcgamer.com/cruelty-squad-review/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
| Destruct = 7.5/10<ref>{{cite news |last1=Handley |first1=Zoey |title=Review: Cruelty Squad |url=https://www.destructoid.com/reviews/review-cruelty-squad/ |website=[[Destructoid]] |date=19 June 2021 |access-date=25 November 2021 |archive-date=10 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610130035/https://www.destructoid.com/reviews/review-cruelty-squad/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
| MC = 89/100<ref name="MCPC">{{Cite web|url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/cruelty-squad/critic-reviews/?platform=pc|title=Cruelty Squad for PC Reviews|website=[[Metacritic]]|access-date=June 16, 2022}}</ref>
}}

''Cruelty Squad'' received "generally favorable" reviews, according to [[review aggregator]] website [[Metacritic]].<ref name="MCPC"/>

James Brod of ''Third Coast Review'' described the game as "grislier than ''[[Hotline Miami]]''" and recommended it to fans of "old school tactical shooters".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Brod|first=James|date=2021-03-17|title=Cruelty Squad Early Access Preview: Immersive Sin|url=https://thirdcoastreview.com/2021/03/17/cruelty-squad-early-access-preview-immersive-sin/|access-date=2021-03-31|website=Third Coast Review|language=en-US|archive-date=2022-06-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610130035/https://thirdcoastreview.com/2021/03/17/cruelty-squad-early-access-preview-immersive-sin/|url-status=live}}</ref> Jake Tucker of ''[[NME]]'' declared ''Cruelty Squad'' to be the "most compelling game of the year", awarding it five stars out of five.<ref name="NME">{{Cite web |last=Tucker |first=Jake |date=2021-07-05 |title='Cruelty Squad' review - An anti-capitalist screed that's the most compelling game of the year |url=https://www.nme.com/reviews/game-reviews/cruelty-squad-review-2985724 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610130036/https://www.nme.com/reviews/game-reviews/cruelty-squad-review-2985724 |archive-date=2022-06-10 |access-date=2021-07-06 |website=[[NME]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> Many outlets also commented on the harshness of the visuals, with ''[[Rock Paper Shotgun]]''{{'s}} Graham Smith dubbing them "sensorally aggressive".<ref name="RPS">{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=Graham |date=2021-06-19 |title=Cruelty Squad is 'an immersive power fantasy simulator set in a sewage infused garbage world' |language=en |work=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]] |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/cruelty-squad-is-an-immersive-power-fantasy-simulator-set-in-a-sewage-infused-garbage-world |url-status=live |access-date=2021-07-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210710002026/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/cruelty-squad-is-an-immersive-power-fantasy-simulator-set-in-a-sewage-infused-garbage-world |archive-date=2021-07-10}}</ref> James Davenport of ''[[PC Gamer]]'' called it "some prime existential PC gaming horror."<ref name="PCGamer rev" />

In June 2021, the protagonist of ''Cruelty Squad'' was added to the video game ''[[Brigador]]'' as a playable character, under the name "MT Foxtrot".<ref>{{Citation |title=The Blood Anniversary Update Is Now Live |date=June 7, 2021 |url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/274500/view/3077625729414684577 |website=[[Steam (service)|Steam]] |access-date=June 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210817005814/https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/274500/view/3077625729414684577 |url-status=live |language=en |archive-date=August 17, 2021}}</ref>
